chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Ibn al-Yasa', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not make eating fish a habit, for it melts the body.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.تُدْمِنُوا: Make a habit / become accustomed to

ai.seo_question: What is the health benefit or ruling regarding habitual fish consumption in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, links the dietary advice of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) directly to Imam Ali (a.s.), highlighting the continuity of prophetic wisdom in Shia tradition. The phrase 'yuthib al-jasad' (melts the body) is interpreted by scholars as indicating the reduction of bodily strength and vitality, serving as a practical guideline for maintaining physical robustness through moderation rather than abstinence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, from Ibn Al Yas’a,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not be habitual in eating the fish for it melts the body’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah from ibn al-Yasa‘ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘
Do not eat fish very often; it melts the body.’”
